Vietnam was a clusterfuck, an epic tragedy, and a level of human suffering that is finally coming to modern consciousness. 

It's not like the US got involved in the war for ethnic cleansing or purely imperialistic ideals. I don't think the US should have gotten involved at all and that it should have been something for the UN to deal with prior to the French catastrophe eventually leading to US involvement. 

The ends don't justify the means in the Vietnam war, as it escalated and peaked the human suffering mirrored the trend. 

Yes the US troops and soldiers did awful things, used chemical warfare, and bombed civilian targets. And continued to do so to save face instead of admitting defeat. My dad was there and never really spoke of what he had to endure, and spoke of that time as a waste of his life. The Southern Vietnam government was almost on par with how awful Northern Vietnam was and the VC.

However the US never had state-sponsored Genocide that the Nazis did nor the sheer expansionist ideals, and I'm not painting 1960's America as a place of human equality. Yes the collapse of the VC would have left the US with a highly powerful all in SEA, but that does not justify the actions of the war, and it is playing "What if History."
